title: Varna 4. The Account of the Discussion of Brahman
html:
In the eastern country Jagadisha teaches the shastras to brahmanas' sons and makes them Vaishnavas; the pandit Vidyanidhi Bhattacharya, who holds that Brahman is formless, comes to debate with him; the story of Hanuman's doubt and the voice from the effulgent abode; the testimony of the Bhagavata, the Brahma-vaivarta Purana, the Bhagavad-gita and the Padma Purana; Vidyanidhi takes shelter of Jagadisha and attains Krishna-prema

The fourth varna

1Glory, glory to Jagadisha, glory to the merciful one!
Be kind and show mercy to me, a wretch.

2I am a man poor, lowly and bad, sunk in base worldly pursuits;
fallen, destitute, and an utter wretch besides.

3In a dream I received Bhagavatananda's command;
by the strength of that command, Prabhu, I sing your virtues.

4Mercifully be pleased with me, a fallen one,
so that somehow the description of [your] life may be completed.

5The pastimes Prabhu performed while living in the eastern country —
all those pastimes I have written down in this book.

6When the holy upanayana had been performed, Prabhu with a joyful heart
began to teach various shastras to the sons of brahmanas.

7The brahmanas' sons whom Prabhu taught the shastras,
having come to know the truth of bhakti, all became teachers.

8Thus many brahmanas from various lands,1
coming to Prabhu, study [under him].

9One studies grammar and lexicons;
another studies the science of literature (sahitya-shastra).

10Some study smriti and logic, some Vedanta;
some fortunate one studies shruti, the Vedas and the agamas.

11Thus the disciples study various shastras;
by Prabhu's mercy everyone's mind is at Krishna's feet.

12After the various shastras, at the end he teaches the Puranas;
some study the Sri Bhagavata.

13Learning from it the determination of all truths,
by Prabhu's mercy all became Vaishnavas.

14Thus Jagadisha teaches his disciples;
seeing [this], mother and father rejoiced at heart.

15The Bandya says: "Bhagyavati, this is your good fortune:
therefore this saintly son was born from your womb."

16Bhagyavati says: "My lord, by your mercy
a son devoted to Krishna was born from my womb."2

17Kamalaksha and Bhagyavati, sitting in their house,
always speak of their son's virtues with joy at heart.

18Meanwhile Jagadisha here teaches his disciples
and with his disciples performs Hari-sankirtana.

19Rising early in the morning, Prabhu performs sankirtana —
and at that time a brahmana's son came.

20He was a man of great learning, expert in every branch of knowledge;
the learned of all lands yielded to him.

21Having heard with his own ears of Prabhu's learning,
he came into Prabhu's presence to debate the shastras.

22His renowned name was Vidyanidhi Bhattacharya;
his gift of poetry equalled that of Kalidasa.3

23Having defeated the pandits of all lands,
he came and appeared where Jagadisha was.

24Coming, he raised discussion of various shastras:
smriti, logic, Vedanta and the rest — all he debated.

25In the debate on all the shastras he was defeated;
then he raised the question of the inquiry into Brahman.

26Vidyanidhi says: "Brahman is formless."
Prabhu says: "You do not know that Brahman indeed has form."

27Vidyanidhi says: "I know Brahman to be formless:
all the shastras declare It formless.

Tatha hi, in the shastra:

28'[Brahman] is spotless, formless, Its form is effulgence; all the gods are Its parts' — so Rama said to Hanuman long ago.4

29In the Treta-yuga Ramachandra, having bound the ocean,
performed worship, installing a Shiva-linga.5

30Seeing this, Hanuman reflects:
'Whom does Rama, the complete Brahman, worship?

31I know only this: Ramachandra is the complete Brahman.
Now I surmise that there must be another Brahman.'

32This doubt arose in Hanuman's mind;
Ramachandra, the Indweller, knew of it.

33With a smiling face Bhagavan says to Hanuman:
'What are you pondering in your heart, child Hanuman?'

34Hanuman says: 'Lord, You are above all;
whom You worship, this I cannot understand.

35I know: Ramachandra is the Maker, above all,
the beginningless Purusha, the sustainer of all the universes.

36Whom then do You worship? — a doubt has arisen;
this lila of Yours I could not understand.

37Whom does the merciful Lord worship?
Be kind and tell me, have pity.'

38Ramachandra says: 'Child, hear the essence:
the root of all is the effulgent, formless Brahman.

39Its part is Sadashiva, who comprises all the gods;
know for certain: him I worship.'

40Ramachandra — an avatara, Bhagavan in full —
Himself said that the original Brahman is formless.

41According to which shastra do you speak of another Brahman?
Set it out in detail before me."

42Jagadisha says: "You explain to me:
by what was Hanuman's doubt removed?"

43The brahmana says: "Of that I know nothing at all;
I accept only the effulgent, formless Brahman.

44If you know it, then declare:
what is the form of the complete Brahman, Bhagavan?"

45Then Jagadisha says: "Hear, then, the essence:
that effulgent Brahman is the vibhuti of Sri Rama.6

46In the very story you have brought before me
lies its true conclusion (siddhanta).

47Sri Rama said that there is an effulgent Brahman;
hearing this, doubt arose in Hanuman's mind.

48To dispel that doubt, Hanuman
went to where the effulgent abode is.

49Going there, he asked: 'Listen, effulgent one,
tell me the truth about yourself.

50I am the son of the Wind, the servant of Sri Rama;
I have come here to know the truth about you.

51I adjure you by Rama: do not deceive me;
set out the whole truth about yourself.'

52As soon as he said this, from the effulgent abode
a voice issued forth thus:

53'That Rama whose servant you are, from whom the three gunas arose,
from whom creation and the rest come forth — I am only His supreme vibhuti.

54That Rama whose servant you are, O son of the Wind —
from Him the three gunas arose.

55Creation and all the rest come from Him;
know for certain: I am His vibhuti.

56Raghuvara called Himself Brahman:
He is the master of the world, the Ishvara of all.

57To test your mind He beguiled you;
deceived by the ruse, you have come here.

58Go quickly and take hold of Sri Rama's feet —
this is my request to you.

59Doubt arose in you: whom does Rama worship?
Rama Himself worshipped Himself.'

60Hearing the voice from heaven, the great Hanuman,
delighted at heart, reflects:

61'This effulgent Brahman is the vibhuti of Sri Rama;
Sri Rama is the supreme Brahman: I have grasped the essence.'

62Having thus become certain, the heroic lord of monkeys
came back from there with great speed.

63Coming, the hero bowed down at Sri Rama's feet;
the Lord, taking hold of Hanuman, embraced him.

64Then the hero Hanuman, before Sri Rama,
with joined palms began to offer prayers:

65'I have committed an offence at Your feet;
forgive the fault — I am Your foolish servant.

66I am poor and lowly, an animal, a monkey by birth;
be merciful to me, a fallen one, O ocean of compassion!

67Through the confusion of my mind I could not understand;
it has gone away, Lord, by Your compassion.'

68Thus Sri Hanuman's error was removed:
he understood that the formless is Sri Rama's vibhuti.

69You are a pandit, yet you do not know Ishvara;
accept that the effulgence of Ishvara's body is Brahman.7

70In the four yugas Bhagavan has four avataras;
the proof of this is in the Srimad Bhagavata.

Tatha hi, in the Tenth Canto:

71He has taken forms according to the yugas and formerly had three colours —
white, red and yellow; now He has assumed the black.8

72In the four yugas the Lord descends as a complete avatara;
the effulgent Brahman is the radiance of that Lord's body.

73In the Dvapara-yuga Sri Krishna descends as the complete Brahman;
sattva, rajas and tamas arose through His portions.

74That Lord is all that is, the sustainer of all;
apart from Him the world has no other Maker.

Tatha hi, in the Sri Brahma-vaivarta Purana, the words of Sri Mahadeva to Sri Parvati:

75From Brahma down to a blade of grass, all is false, O Parvati;
worship the true, supreme Brahman — the Lord of Radha, who is beyond the three gunas.9

76Shiva says: 'Gauri, hear my words:
with undivided mind always worship Sri Krishna's feet.

77The Lord, the Master of Radhika, is beyond the three gunas;
apart from the feet of that Lord there is no other refuge.

78From Brahma down to a blade of grass, all is impermanent;
Sri Krishna, eternity, knowledge and bliss, is the supreme Brahman, the truth.

79Whoever leaves such a Krishnachandra and worships another
is bewildered by maya and steeped in utter ignorance.'

80Shiva — lord of the three worlds, god of the gods —
says that Krishna is Brahman, the Maker of all.

81Leaving such a Brahman, you call Brahman formless;
I know: your learning lies in invented shastras."

82Hearing this, the brahmana bowed his head;
Jagadisha again began to speak to him:

83"Listen, brahmana: Vedavyasa wrote in the Purana
what Parvati told King Suratha.10

Tatha hi, in the Sri Brahma-vaivarta Purana, in the Prakriti-khanda:

84From Brahma down to a blade of grass, all is perishable;
eternal and true is the supreme Brahman — Krishna, beyond the gunas, the Infallible.

85From Brahma down to a blade of grass, all is perishable;
eternal and true is the supreme Brahman — Krishna, the Lord of all.

86All that you see in the universe is the making of maya;
from Krishna's maya come Brahma and the other gods.

87Krishna, beyond the gunas, the Infallible, is the father of all,
the Creator of all, the Destroyer of all, the Protector of all.

88Parvati, O brahmana, told Suratha this truth;
the Devi instructed [him] to worship Sri Krishna.11

89The king says: 'Mother, I do not know Krishna;
you are the maker of the universe, the mother of the three gunas.'

90The Devi says: 'Listen attentively, O king:
what you have said is not untrue.

Tatha hi, in the same place:

91I am the original of Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva and the rest, higher than the highest,
with qualities and beyond qualities, the best, ever acting by my own will.

92I am manifold: by a portion and by maya I am all women;
and I, O king, was created by Krishna through the play of His eyebrows.

93Through the play of His eyebrows He created the great Virat among purushas,
in the pores of whose skin the universes eternally abide.12

94I am the original of Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva and the rest,
with qualities and beyond qualities, higher than the highest, acting by my own will.

95Through kalas and amshas I take many forms;
all women are my own form.

96Such as I am, Vamshidhara created me
through the play of His eyebrows — know this, O best of kings.

97This you have heard; now I shall tell you something more:
the Virat Purusha is an avatara of Maha-Vishnu.

98Him Krishna created through the play of His eyebrows;
in the pores of His skin this universe ever abides.'

99The conversation that took place between Parvati and King Suratha —
that conversation I have now told you.

100I shall tell something more, best of brahmanas — you listen:
what Arjuna said to Sri Krishna.

Tatha hi, in the Srimad Bhagavad-gita, in the eleventh chapter:

101You are the original God, the ancient Purusha, You are the supreme refuge of this universe. You are the knower and the knowable, and the supreme abode; by You the universe is pervaded, O You of endless forms.13

102You are Vayu, Yama, Agni, Varuna, the moon, Prajapati and the great-grandsire. Obeisance, obeisance to You a thousand times, and again, and yet again — obeisance, obeisance to You!

103Obeisance to You from in front and from behind, obeisance to You from every side, O All! Infinite is Your might, immeasurable Your valour; You pervade all, and therefore You are all.

104The original Purusha of all the gods, the Ancient One,
You are the place where this universe dissolves.14

105You are the support of the world, the one thing to be known;
You are that very cause, manifest before the eyes in form.15

106You alone have pervaded this universe;
bearer of endless forms, You are beyond perception.

107Vayu, Yama, Agni, Varuna, the lord of the night;
the father of Brahma's father — who can understand Your ways?16

108Obeisance, obeisance, O Mahaprabhu, obeisance again and again,
thousands upon thousands of times, again and again — obeisance.17

109Your power is immeasurable, no one can measure it;
You abide in all beings, within and without.

110Gold is one — the difference lies in the shaping of many forms:
You are all forms, as the Veda says."

111This is what Arjuna said in the Bharata;
hearing it, the brahmana's mind was turned.

112He bows down to Jagadisha [prostrate] with eight limbs
and says: "Deliver me, placing your feet on my head."

113Prabhu says: "Why do you speak to me in this way?
Worship Sri Krishna, leaving the formless.

114Apart from Krishna the living being has no other refuge;
with one mind worship His feet."

115The brahmana says: "I have understood: you are a part of Krishna.18
Be merciful: I take shelter of you.

116By your mercy my evil-mindedness has been shattered;
Prabhu, teach me what is to be done and what is not.

117I have no knowledge of the truth, I am wicked;
your descent is to make the living beings know the truth."

Tatha hi:

118To those whose minds are drawn by sense objects he gives knowledge of the truth;
Sri Jagadisha, the very form of Ishvara, I worship day and night.

119"All the living beings whose minds are drawn by sense objects
have fallen into the well of worldly existence.

120Taking pity on those beings, Prabhu,
you delivered them, giving knowledge of the truth.

121You are the very form of Ishvara, a treasure-house of mercy;
have mercy: [let me] serve your feet without cease.

122Bring me to the goal of life, giving me the shade of your feet;
in compassion make me know the truth of Sri Krishna.

123Be merciful, Jagadisha, deliverer of the world:
apart from your lotus feet there is no other refuge."

124Saying this, the brahmana fell at Prabhu's feet;
Prabhu embraced him with a merciful heart.

125Comforting him, Prabhu seated him at his side
and speaks to him words for his good in the sweetest tones.

126Prabhu says: "Listen, O son of a brahmana:
whoever, born a human being, does not worship Krishna —

127his birth is wasted, in vain he comes and goes;
I count such a fallen wretch among the beasts."

Tatha hi, in the Sri Padma Purana:

128Even a chandala devoted to bhakti for Vishnu is the best of sages;
and a twice-born devoid of bhakti for Vishnu is lower than a dog-eater.

129A chandala becomes the best if he is a devotee of Krishna;
a brahmana is called low if he does not worship Krishna.

130Thus in the Uttara-khanda the great Shiva,
the lord, tells Parvati the truth of Krishna.

131Hearing this, the brahmana's son says:
"Be merciful to me: my days are passing in vain."

132Then Jagadisha Prabhu showed great mercy:
he explained to him all the teaching on the truth of Krishna.

133Having obtained Krishna-prema and bhakti, that best of the twice-born,
his life fulfilled, went to his own home.

134In this way Jagadisha, establishing bhakti,
delivered all worldly people.

135The life of Jagadisha is made of millions of oceans of nectar;
were it described in detail, the book would grow beyond measure.

136For fear of enlarging the book, I have written briefly;
the discussion of Brahman I have described here in brief.

137Srila Bhagavatananda Prabhu is full of mercy;
this Ananda places hope in his feet.

138In a dream that Prabhu commanded [me] by a revelation (pratyadesha);
by the strength of his command I have described a little.

Thus in the Charitra-vijaya of Sri Jagadisha Pandita ends the fourth varna, called "The Account of the Discussion of Brahman".

Notes

  1. The edition reads «বহুবিপ্র দান»; «দান» is taken as «গণ» (gaṇa), "many brahmanas" (rhyming with «অধ্যয়ন»). The reading is unclear.
  2. «প্রভু» (prabhu) is here a wife's address to her husband.
  3. Vidyanidhi Bhattacharya is not to be confused with Pundarika Vidyanidhi, the associate of Sri Chaitanya.
  4. The verse and the story that follows (29–39) are Vidyanidhi's argument; his speech continues to 41. The source of the verse and of the story of Hanuman's doubt has not been identified.
  5. "Having bound the ocean" (samudra bandiyā) — having built the bridge to Lanka; by tradition Rama installed a Shiva-linga at Rameshvaram before this.
  6. Vibhuti (vibhūti) — a manifestation of the Lord's power, His possession.
  7. Cf. Brahma-samhita 5.40 and CC Adi 1–2: the impersonal Brahman spoken of in the Upanishads is the effulgence of the Lord's body.
  8. Bhagavata 10.8.13 — the words of Garga Muni to Nanda Maharaja about Krishna.
  9. The edition has «শিয়্যৈব»; taken as «মিথ্যৈব» (mithyaiva), "all is false"; cf. the paraphrase in 78 («সকলি অনিত্য»). Stamba is a tuft of grass; the paraphrase (78) has «স্তম্ভ», "pillar".
  10. Suratha is a king, a worshipper of Durga (cf. the Devi-mahatmya of the Markandeya Purana); here Parvati instructs him in the worship of Krishna.
  11. «পার্বতী সুরথ বিপ্রে এ তত্ত্ব কহিল» — bipre is taken as an address to the brahmana (Vidyanidhi); literally "to the brahmana Suratha" is also possible, but in 83, 89, 96 and 99 Suratha is a king.
  12. «নিত্য সর» (nitya sara) at the end of the verse is taken as nityaśaḥ, "constantly, eternally"; the reading is unclear. In the edition the verse ends with a single danda.
  13. Bhagavad-gita 11.38–40 (101–103).
  14. «এই ভবিশ্বের হও পরলয় স্থান» is taken as «এই ত বিশ্বের… প্রলয়-স্থান» (pralaya-sthāna), "the place of dissolution of [this] universe"; cf. viśvasya paraṁ nidhānam (101).
  15. «পরতেক» (paratek) is taken as pratyakṣa, "before the eyes"; pratyeka, "in each", is also possible. The reading is unclear.
  16. A paraphrase of prapitāmaha (102): Brahma is the "grandsire" (pitāmaha) of the world, and the Lord is his father.
  17. Mahaprabhu ("the Great Lord") is here Arjuna's address to Krishna.
  18. The brahmana glorifies Jagadisha as "a part of Krishna" (115), a "descent" (117) and "the very form of Ishvara" (118, 121). According to the teaching of the Gaudiya Vaishnavas, Jagadisha Pandita is an eternal associate of the Lord (in Krishna-lila, according to GGD 143, Chandrahasa, a dancer of Vraja); a devotee is honoured in this way as the Lord's dear servant: "All the shastras call [the guru] Hari Himself…, but he is the Lord's dear [servant]" (sākṣād-dharitvena samasta-śāstrair uktaḥ… kintu prabhor yaḥ priya eva tasya, Gurvashtaka 7).
